title: The Ad Agency That Ran a 'Hate Your Job' Campaign to Sell Pills
hook: A pharmaceutical company paid millions to make you miserable at work — just so you'd buy their antidepressant.
why_this_can_go_viral: Reveals a hidden system where a brand deliberately worsened your mental state for profit — triggering outrage and shares.

title: The CEO Who Sold His Own Company's Secrets to a Rival — Twice
hook: He betrayed his own board, pocketed millions, and when they caught him, they hired him back.
why_this_can_go_viral: Betrayal stories are inherently viral; adding the absurd twist of rehiring the traitor shocks viewers.

title: The Startup That Used 'Fake Employees' to Trick Investors into Funding $50M
hook: They hired actors to sit in empty cubicles — and the investors never visited the office.
why_this_can_go_viral: Visual absurdity of paid actors pretending to work makes for a shareable, shocking story.

title: The Monopoly That Bought Every Funeral Home — Then Tripled the Price of Dying
hook: One corporation now controls 20% of all funerals in America — and they're charging grieving families 300% more.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines universal fear (death) with universal anger (price gouging) — high emotional resonance.

title: The Factory That Faked Its Entire Supply Chain — Even the Address Was a Vacant Lot
hook: They sold products 'made in Italy' that were actually assembled in a shed in Bangladesh.
why_this_can_go_viral: Reveals a hidden layer of deception in everyday products — viewers will question everything they own.

title: The Doctor Who Was Paid $500,000 to Say a Poison Was Medicine
hook: A pharmaceutical company secretly paid a respected physician to endorse a drug that killed 100 people.
why_this_can_go_viral: Doctors are trusted figures; revealing they were bought triggers deep distrust and shares.

title: The Hedge Fund That Leaked Fake News to Tank a Rival — Then Bought Its Remains
hook: They planted a false story, watched the stock crash, and acquired the company for pennies on the dollar.
why_this_can_go_viral: Ties current distrust of 'fake news' to financial crime — feels like a real-life financial thriller.

title: The Coffee Brand That Paid Homeless Shelters to Refuse Entry to Its Rival's Customers
hook: They didn't compete on taste — they made sure your only option was theirs by controlling the streets.
why_this_can_go_viral: Extreme real-world ruthlessness that feels like a movie plot — shocking and deeply unfair.

title: The CEO Who Faked His Own Death — and Ran the Company from a Grave
hook: He was declared dead, but continued sending emails to the board from beyond the grave for 18 months.
why_this_can_go_viral: Absurd, unbelievable, and almost comedic — perfect for dramatic storytelling across platforms.

title: The Oil Company That Dumped Toxic Waste in a Village's Only Well — Then Blamed the Villagers
hook: They poisoned an entire community's water supply and sued the families for 'trespassing' when they tried to leave.
why_this_can_go_viral: Pure injustice + environmental horror. Activists and concerned consumers will amplify it.

title: The Startup That Voted Itself a Billion-Dollar Valuation — With Fake Shareholders
hook: They created 50 fake email accounts to approve their own valuation — and almost got away with it.
why_this_can_go_viral: Shows how easy it is to fake a billion-dollar company — makes viewers skeptical of every 'unicorn'.

title: The Hotel Chain That Installed Cameras in Rooms — and Livestreamed Guests for Profit
hook: They made millions by selling access to a secret channel that showed guests in their most private moments.
why_this_can_go_viral: Maximum darkness + maximum personal relevance. Every hotel guest will feel violated and share.

title: The Sugar Lobby That Secretly Funded a 'Science' Institute to Say Sugar Is Safe
hook: They paid a Harvard professor to write a 'study' that blamed fat instead — and it became national policy.
why_this_can_go_viral: Ties to obesity epidemic — people want to know who to blame. Historical manipulation is infuriating.

title: The Man Who Built a 'Fake Amazon' — and Sold 50,000 Fake Products Before Anyone Noticed
hook: He copied Amazon's entire interface, tricked suppliers, and shipped empty boxes for 11 months.
why_this_can_go_viral: Bizarre and audacious — viewers love stories of massive deception that almost succeeded.

title: The Pharma Giant That Hid a Cancer-Causing Ingredient for 15 Years
hook: They knew the 'inactive ingredient' caused tumors — and quietly changed the formula only after a lawsuit.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines health fear with corporate betrayal — everyone who took the drug will share.

title: The Bank That Bought a Town — Then Foreclosed on Every Home in It
hook: They acquired the entire municipality, then systematically evicted every family to build a data center.
why_this_can_go_viral: An entire town destroyed by one corporation — feels like a dystopian horror story come true.

title: The Ad Buyer Who Bid $0.01 on a Rival's Brand Name — and Stole All Their Customers
hook: He spent $12 to redirect a competitor's entire ad budget to his own site — using a single line of code.
why_this_can_go_viral: Reveals a hidden vulnerability in digital ads — business owners will share out of fear.

title: The Spy Who Spent 10 Years as a Janitor — and Stole Nuclear Secrets for a Rival Nation
hook: He mopped floors for a decade, memorized classified documents, and walked out with 50,000 pages in his bucket.
why_this_can_go_viral: Stealth + patience = incredible story. The 'invisible worker' angle is deeply compelling.

title: The Company That Patented the Color Orange — and Sued Every Competitor Who Used It
hook: They owned a color — and used it to destroy 200 smaller brands that dared to sell orange products.
why_this_can_go_viral: Absurdly unfair — viewers will side with the little guys and rage-share the injustice.

title: The Recruiter Who Built a 'Ghost Employee' Army — and Collected $8M in Fake Salaries
hook: He hired 300 people who didn't exist, paid them into his own accounts, and no one checked for 4 years.
why_this_can_go_viral: The audacity of the scheme is entertaining — viewers love 'how did they get away with it' stories.

title: The Tire Company That Knew Its Tires Explode at 60 MPH — and Sold 2 Million Anyway
hook: Internal memos showed the defect, but they calculated that paying lawsuits was cheaper than a recall.
why_this_can_go_viral: Everyone drives — this is a direct safety threat. Outrage and fear drive massive engagement.

title: The Founder Who Sold 'Founder Status' to 500 People — All Thinking They Were the CEO
hook: He sold 500 'CEO' titles to investors — each believing they were the sole owner of the company.
why_this_can_go_viral: Absurd and hilarious but also dark — the 'how did 500 people not talk to each other' question sells.

title: The Meat Supplier That Mixed Rat Poison into Sausages — to 'Preserve' Them Longer
hook: They discovered that a banned chemical kept meat 'fresh' for months — and used it until children started dying.
why_this_can_go_viral: Extreme physical danger + food you eat daily. Instant horror + personal relevance = viral.

title: The Hedge Fund That Paid a Weatherman to Fake a Hurricane Forecast — and Short an Insurance Stock
hook: A single fake weather report tanked an insurance company's stock — and the fund made $400 million in 24 hours.
why_this_can_go_viral: Blends weather, finance, and conspiracy — a perfect storm of curiosity and outrage.
